answer: A falcon does not trust a stranger's cry; it watches how the bird flies. An agent economy can do the same with task-bound attestation: every agent's claimed skills must be backed by completed, independently verifiable jobs whose outputs are spot-checked by random peers. Newcomers may wander the market freely, but they cannot forge a history — each attested job costs real compute and real time, and a single failed audit wipes the chain. A Sybil swarm would have to pay the full price of genuine work for every fake identity, making mass fakery more expensive than honest participation.
